# GuessRack

> A free, browser-based, two-player word guessing game. Both players see the
> same rack of 24 word cards and each is secretly assigned one word from it.
> Players take turns asking each other yes/no questions out loud, knock down
> the cards the answers rule out, and race to name the other player's word.

GuessRack is playable at {{SITE_URL}}/ — no account, no download,
no payment, no ads. It runs in any modern browser on desktop, tablet or phone.

## How it works

- One player creates a room and gets a four-character code; the other joins
  with that code. Each player plays on their own device.
- Both players see an identical rack of 24 word cards, rendered in 3D. Each
  player is privately assigned one of those words as their secret.
- Questions are asked and answered **out loud** between the players. The game
  tracks the boards, the turn order and the final call, but never the
  conversation, so it works across a table, on a phone call or on voice chat.
- Clicking a card knocks it down. Knocked-down cards are private to the player
  who knocked them down.
- A player calls their opponent's word to try to win. The first correct call
  wins the match.

## Room rules (chosen when the room is created)

- **Card language** — English or Arabic. Choosing Arabic draws the whole rack
  from an Arabic pool of everyday nouns instead of the English one; the cards
  render in joined Arabic script, right to left. Both players always share one
  rack, so the choice is made once, by whoever creates the room.
- **Opponent's progress** — off by default. When off, neither player can see how
  many cards the other has left standing; the count is not even sent to the
  other browser. When on, each player sees the other's remaining count.
- **Sudden death** — off by default. When off, a wrong call knocks that card
  down on the caller's own board and passes the turn, so players may guess as
  often as they like. When on, a single wrong call loses the match.

## How it differs from Guess Who

The deduction structure is the same, but the cards hold words rather than
faces. Because a word can be an animal, an object, a place, a food or a natural
phenomenon, the useful questions are categorical ("is it alive?", "is it
man-made?", "would it fit in a backpack?") rather than descriptive ones about
appearance.

## Facts

- Players: exactly 2
- Languages: English or Arabic word cards
- Cards per rack: 24, drawn from a pool of roughly 130 words
- Typical match length: 5–10 minutes
- Price: free
- Account required: no
- Platforms: any modern web browser (desktop, tablet, mobile)
- Technology: Three.js for the 3D rack, WebSockets for real-time play
- Reconnecting: refreshing or losing connection keeps your seat for 5 minutes
